findings.title: Get-PrivateKeys PowerShell function exported machine certificate private keys to password-protected .pfx files on SCRANTON
findings.summary: On scranton.dmevals.local, in the session of user DMEVALS\pbeesly, a PowerShell script block named Get-PrivateKeys (ScriptBlock ID 9d153741-75c3-4062-afe3-aeca0aee611b, logged with Path C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\readme.ps1) enumerated every certificate in cert:\LocalMachine recursively and called Export-PfxCertificate for each certificate with a thumbprint, writing the private-key-bearing .pfx to $env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<random>.pfx protected by the hardcoded password "saribas". The function was invoked at 2020-05-02T03:04:56Z (script block 'Get-PrivateKeys', PID 3876) and at 03:04:57.460Z Sysmon recorded the resulting file C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\coyn5igj.3io.pfx created by powershell.exe (PID 3876). This is direct theft of authentication certificate private keys from the local machine store, matching T1649. The activity sits inside a broader intrusion chain on the same host: at 02:58:44Z a hidden, execution-policy-bypassing PowerShell (parent control.exe /name Microsoft.BackupAndRestoreCenter) decoded a payload from C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\monkey.png via System.Drawing pixel extraction and IEX'd it; at 03:08:51Z a second PowerShell (PID 3852) ran an Invoke-BeachCleanup function (Path C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\psversion.ps1) that deleted Downloads\*.pfx, *.bmp, *.png and %APPDATA%\OfficeSupplies.7z, and Sysmon event 23 confirms coyn5igj.3io.pfx was deleted at 03:08:51.489Z by DMEVALS\pbeesly. The export-then-wipe pattern indicates deliberate exfiltration staging and anti-forensics. No certificate-based (PKINIT) authentication was observed: all 14 Kerberos 4768 TGT requests in windows.security show PreAuthType 2 (password pre-auth) with Status 0x0, and the single SystemCertificates registry modification (4657 on nashua.dmevals.local, ROOT\Certificates\BE36A4562FB2EE05DBB3D32323ADF445084ED656, by NASHUA$) is not linked to this activity. Zeek x509/kerberos data (2020-04-30) does not overlap the Windows window and shows only AS/TGS requests with KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED, no certificate-auth anomalies.
